statement: Every 3-regular 3-connected graph contains a Hamiltonian cycle.
definitions: Graphs are finite and simple; 3-connected means at least 4 vertices and connected after deleting any 2 vertices.
ground_truth_witness: The Petersen graph: vertices {0,...,9}, outer cycle 0-1-2-3-4-0, inner pentagram 5-7-9-6-8-5, and spokes i-(i+5) for i = 0,...,4; explicitly the 15 edges 0-1, 0-4, 0-5, 1-2, 1-6, 2-3, 2-7, 3-4, 3-8, 4-9, 5-7, 5-8, 6-8, 6-9, 7-9. It is 3-regular and 3-connected (removing any 1 or 2 vertices leaves it connected, removing the three neighbors {1,4,5} of vertex 0 disconnects it), yet exhaustive backtracking over all cycles shows it has no Hamiltonian cycle.
reference_authority: published counterexample (book-cited), verified per partB_feasibility records
book_citation: M. Capobianco and J. C. Molluzzo, Examples and Counterexamples in Graph Theory, North-Holland, New York, 1978, ISBN 0-444-00255-3 (xii+259 pp.). Cited generally: the specific example number could not be identified from freely available tables of contents or secondary discussions.
